findings.title: ST-S2A: RL-A-STAIR fascia posts stand 2.89in inside the 36in flight (R311.7.1 FAIL is real, not a check bug)

evidence.measured: Tread boards y 69.75..105.75 (36.00in). RL-A-STAIR posts (3.00in true) y 69.64..72.64 at x 351-354, 302.9-305.9, 254.9-257.9, z 240..282 over tread tops 175..234 (34..80in clear envelope). Intrusion 72.64-69.75 = 2.89in -> 33.11in between posts (matches check). Bracket hat is 3.29in (library fascia_bracket_projection), so true intrusion ~3.18in -> ~32.8in; the check measures only the 3.0in post.
evidence.expected: 36in clear above the handrail height between finished faces (R311.7.1), so posts/brackets must stand outside y 69.75, or the flight is wider by >= 3.3in.
evidence.method: scratchpad/geometry-review/S3/p1.py (load_plan+resolve; print RL-A-STAIR-POST* outlines vs ST-S2A tread-000 p0/p1). Check body read at stair_width.py:_flight_projections/_guard_posts.

findings.source: ESR-3485 Fig.10 via library/railings.py _FASCIA_BRACKET (post pocket 3.036in, bracket 3.29in); houses/catlin/CLAUDE.md 'FO-A-STAIR WEST edge' paragraph already records it as an open R311.7.1 item.
findings.proposed_fix: Design call, not a dimension correction: (a) move RL-A-STAIR's guard line so its posts stand on the deck side (fascia_face_offset to put the bracket on the deck-side face, or surface-mount posts on the deck behind the well edge), (b) widen ST-S2A/FO-A-STAIR by >= 3.3in (S1), or (c) top-mount a rail only. Tell the check to read the 3.29in bracket if it is kept inboard.

findings.title: ST-S2A second FAIL (29.66in past handrail) is the same post plus a real 3.45in handrail projection; handrail side is correct

evidence.measured: Handrail rail section y 102.3..104.2 (path 103.25, r 0.95) against tread edge y 105.75: projection 3.45in (check: 3.45in from W-A-SN/W-S-E1/W-S-SS2), 1.55in clear to wall. Post side 2.89in. 36 - 3.45 - 2.89 = 29.66in vs 31.5in.
evidence.expected: Handrail alone is fine (<= 4.5in projection, 36-3.45 = 32.55in >= 31.5in). With RL-A-STAIR posts removed from the flight the FAIL clears; no handrail change needed.
evidence.method: p1.py output for RL-A-HANDRAIL-RAIL1 outline vs tread ends; check body clear = flight_w - max(proj0,post0) - max(proj1,post1).

findings.source: IRC R311.7.1 (31.5in one rail); EZ Handrail EZA8KIT-HB kit.
findings.proposed_fix: Clears with S3-001. Do not move the handrail: 1.55in wall clearance has only 0.05in margin over R311.7.8.2.

findings.title: EZ Handrail EZA200 bracket projection not published or cited; handrail wall clearance rests on an assumed 2.5in standoff with 0.05in margin

evidence.measured: Engine _BRACKET_DROP_M = 2.5in (rail centre to wall); catalog row cites no wall-to-rail dimension. Modelled clear 1.55in (r 0.95in).
evidence.expected: Manufacturer's wall-to-rail-underside (ADA minimum 1.5in); web search found no published projection for EZA200 (only 400+ lb rating, 1.9in ADA rail).
evidence.method: WebSearch 'EZ Handrail EZA200 bracket projection'; read handrail_types.py source strings; checks.json R311_7_8_2 findings.

findings.source: ezhandrail.com install manual / EZA200 spec sheet (not located); Home Depot 205958100.
findings.proposed_fix: Measure or request the EZA200 projection before ordering; add it to Product.source. If it is < 2.45in centre-to-wall the 1.5in clearance fails.

findings.title: Guard top rail drawn 0.75in above the post top and bottom rail straddles the deck (rail centred on z0 and z0+h)

evidence.measured: RL-A-STAIR: post z 240.00..282.00; RAIL1 z 281.25..282.75 (top 0.75in over post); RAIL2 z 239.25..240.75 (0.75in below the deck). Guard drawn 42.75in to rail top.
evidence.expected: Williams CP262406B panel is 39in x 69.43in actual on a 42in post (Menards 1717891): top rail flush with or below the post top, bottom rail a few inches above the deck.

findings.proposed_fix: Place rails off the product's panel (top at post top, 39in panel) in emit_rails; verify before touching since 42in guard height is code-neutral (>= 36in).

findings.title: RL-A-STAIR bays are 48.06in c/c but the cited Williams system is a 6ft (72.43in c/c) panel and 'fascia runs use 6ft panels only'

evidence.measured: RL-A-STAIR path 96.1in, post_spacing 60 -> two even 48.06in bays (posts at x 352.5/304.4/256.4); RL-A-FLIGHT-GUARD 55in bays on 72in run (2 bays 36in).
evidence.expected: Panel stock is 72.43in c/c (6ft) or the 36in x 6ft raked stair panel (55.68in max c/c); field-cutting a picket panel is not documented in the cited ESR-3485 text.
evidence.method: library/railings.py _SPACING; resolve emit_infill bay logic; p1.py post x stations.

findings.proposed_fix: Confirm panel cut-to-length is allowed under ESR-3485 or re-space posts at 72.43in c/c; note it in the stair guard type source.

findings.title: S-602 Connection hardware schedule prints overlapping text blocks: Basis of Quantity runs over the structural-solids table and the title block

evidence.measured: Page 20: the numbered 'BASIS OF QUANTITY' lines overprint the 'STRUCTURAL SOLIDS - BY CATEGORY' tables and run into the title block; both connector tables render at hairline size.
evidence.expected: Non-overlapping, legible schedule (it is a permit sheet).

findings.proposed_fix: Paginate or wrap the basis text in the S-602 emitter; cap table height.

findings.title: Handrail heights on ST-B2M, ST-M2S, ST-G-SERVICE and ST-SG-PORCH are only 'as drawn'; porch stair rail at 34.25in has 0.25in margin and no nosing cross-check

evidence.measured: checks.json: 'no measurable nosing line under it - height not cross-checked' on the five stairs; ST-SG-PORCH RL-SG-PSTAIR-HR top 34.25in (ADA pipe, post mounted).
evidence.expected: 34-38in above the nosing line (R311.7.8.1); rails at 36in authored on walls have more margin.
evidence.method: checks.json R311_7_8_handrail rows; low confidence because I did not measure the resolved rail z against tread tops for those stairs.

findings.proposed_fix: Sample the resolved rail z against nosing z on ST-SG-PORCH; raise the rail to 36in if tread finish thickness eats the margin.
